IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-inference-pool — multiple CUDA OOMs reported on nodes g-infer-03..05, headroom still showing ~1.2GB free. Escalating to on-call.

Alice M.: I'm on it. seeing higher 5xx from hosted-api in the last 2m. dashboard shows spike in allocation failures.

Ben K.: grabbing logs from g-infer-04. can someone confirm if this is new deploy?

Carla R.: no deploys in last 30m, traffic steady, batching a bit up. I suspect allocator fragmentation + stale kv-cache reservations.

Dave L.: hitting this pattern before — CUDA OOM even with headroom when reserved blocks are still accounted but not actually free. dmesg shows nvlink/page-fault churn.

ML Runtime: reproducible locally with stress test? I can run a quick trace. which model variant?

Alice M.: variant=redwood-v1-7b-qat, seq=1024 heavy embeddings bursts. Model pool on g-infer-04.

Ben K.: paste nvidia-smi and allocator snapshot:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB]
16384 MiB, 12500 MiB
```
Allocator dump (partial):
```
reserved_blocks: 1536MB
active_alloc: 10240MB
headroom_reported: 1200MB
free_fragments: multiple small segments (~8-64MB)
```

Carla R.: that reserved_blocks value looks stale — some processes show reserved but not actually mapped. check /proc/<pid>/smaps and cudaMemGetInfo.

Infra SRE: grabbed `cudaMemGetInfo` from container: free=980MB, total=16384MB -> matches headroom_reported mismatch (980 != 1200). possible double-counting between kv-cache and allocator shadow reservation.

Dave L.: also seeing logs: `Allocator: failed to allocate 256MB: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` even though cudaMemGetInfo reported ~900MB. indicates fragmentation + contiguous allocation requirement.

Alice M.: quick mitigation options: 1) evict KV cache prefixes for cold sessions on that node, 2) restart one problematic container to free reserved blocks, 3) route new requests to fallback smaller model. Thoughts?

Ben K.: evicting KV cache in prod: can we run `infra-ctl kvcache evict --node g-infer-04 --age 5m` ? Will that affect throughput badly?

Infra SRE: Evict command queued, running now. Expect minor latency for active sessions.

IncidentBot: Command acknowledged by infra-ctl, task id t-98123.

Carla R.: while evicting, I'm going to patch allocator to relax contiguous allocation for KV prefetch (experimental). If we need to restart, will coordinate.

ML Runtime: tracing shows KV prefetch holding onto per-shard reservations: `reserve_shadow=512MB` per shard, but actual usage leftover ~0. After kvcache eviction, those shadows should be reclaimed but we need a GC pause.

Dave L.: evict complete. telemetry shows drop in reserved_blocks to ~700MB. headroom cudaMemGetInfo now ~1.8GB. but still seeing OOM on one container (pid 2345).

Ben K.: pid 2345 logs: `prefetch: failed reserve: block not available; fallback to on-demand` then `cublas: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED`.

Alice M.: looks like container-level fragmentation persists — a restart of that container will free slack. rolling restart of container 2345 to drain gracefully. tagging customers in affected list.

Infra SRE: initiating graceful restart: `kubectl rollout restart pod/serve-2345 -n inference --grace-period=30`

Carla R.: while restarting, toggle fallback route: change routing policy to prefer g-infer-06 and reduce max-batch-size on g-infer pool to 8.

IncidentBot: Routing change applied: prefer node g-infer-06 for new sessions.

Dave L.: pod restarted, container came back healthy. allocator snapshot after restart:
```
reserved_blocks: 120MB
active_alloc: 11000MB
free_fragments: fewer but still scattered
cudaMemGetInfo free: 2.1GB
```

Ben K.: 5xxs dropping back to baseline, latency also normalizing.

Alice M.: root cause hypothesis: KV prefetch/shadow reservations accumulated stale entries under bursty workloads; allocator requires large contiguous blocks for some library allocations, fragmentation led to OOM despite aggregate headroom. two contributing bugs: 1) kvcache reserve accounting not promptly reclaimed on eviction, 2) allocator not splintering allocations for large contiguous requests.

Carla R.: followups: file a runtime bug for allocator splintering; add a periodic KV shadow reclaim (force GC after eviction). I'll open PRs.

Infra SRE: change to alerting: add a probe - if cudaMemGetInfo_free > headroom_reported + 200MB then warn (reporting mismatch). also add fragmentation metric: largest_contiguous_block.

ML Runtime: will add a smoke test that simulates heavy prefetch + long tail to catch reserve buildup.

Alice M.: customer impact: small window (~3m) of elevated 5xx and retries for a subset of hosts (hosted-api ephemeral). No long-term data loss. Notifying Support to prepare postmortem.

Ben K.: creating incident ticket INC-20257 with timeline and mitigation steps. assigning Carla R. (root cause) and Infra SRE (mitigation/alerts).

IncidentBot: Incident ticket created: INC-20257.

Dave L.: thumbs up on followups. I'll keep monitoring g-infer pool for 2h and then hand back to regular monitoring.

Alice M.: oncall -> clear. I'll transfer notes to the postmortem doc and ping legal if any customer SLAs hit. good triage team, :party-parrot: 

Carla R.: PRs: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/421 (kvcache-gc), https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/88 (allocator-fallback).

Alice M.: closing thread, will update INC with final RCA once PRs merge. :white_check_mark:
